reconstructed_theorem_text: Theorem: for every measurable space X, probability measures mu and nu on X, g : X -> R, and b in R, assume b >= 0, nu <= ofReal(b) times mu, g >= 0 mu-almost everywhere, Integrable(g,mu), and Integrable(g log(g),mu). Then Ent_nu(g) <= b Ent_mu(g). Domination means nu(A) <= ofReal(b) mu(A) for every measurable A, with masses in the nonnegative extended reals. Ent_m(h) means integral_X h(x) log(h(x)) dm(x) - (integral_X h(x) dm(x)) log(integral_X h(x) dm(x)). Every integral is a real Bochner integral over all X, not an extended-real integral; log(0) = 0. Lean totalizes the Bochner integral by assigning zero when integrability fails. No separate nu-integrability premise is displayed; finite domination transfers the assumed integrability. No energy or fixed-test predicate is a hypothesis of this theorem.
objects: A measurable space X, probability measures mu and nu, real function g, real domination bound b, and entropy values Ent_mu(g), Ent_nu(g).
domains: X is an arbitrary measurable space. mu(X) = nu(X) = 1. g : X -> R; b : R is finite. Measure scaling and comparison concern nonnegative extended-real masses. Entropy is real-valued and all its integrals range over X.
quantifiers: For all X, probability measures mu and nu, g, and b, the displayed assumptions imply the entropy bound. Domination quantifies every measurable set; nonnegativity of g is mu-almost everywhere.
assumptions: mu and nu are probability measures; b >= 0; nu(A) <= ofReal(b) mu(A) for every measurable A; g >= 0 mu-almost everywhere; g and g log(g) are Bochner integrable under mu. No strict positivity or smoothness is assumed.
conclusion: integral_X g log(g) dnu - (integral_X g dnu) log(integral_X g dnu) <= b [integral_X g log(g) dmu - (integral_X g dmu) log(integral_X g dmu)].
scopes: Both entropies concern the same g. The explicit integrability assumptions and almost-everywhere sign are under mu; the conclusion also evaluates entropy under nu. Nu-integrability follows from finite measure domination rather than an additional premise. Real.log(0) = 0; no extended-real entropy is used. The contextual fixed-test definition is not invoked by the target theorem.
constant_dependencies: The multiplier is exactly the given b from nu <= ofReal(b) mu, uniformly for all qualifying g. No further constant occurs.
